10:1.en: These are the descendants of Noah's sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth: children were born to them after the flood.

10:10.en: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

10:11.en: From that land Asshur went out and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,

10:12.en: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; that is the great city.

10:13.en: And Egypt fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, the Naphtuhim,

10:14.en: the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.

10:15.en: Canaan fathered Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth.

10:16.en: the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.

10:17.en: the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.

10:18.en: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Afterward the clans of the Canaanites spread out.

10:19.en: The border of the Canaanites ran from Sidon toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

10:2.en: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

10:20.en: These are the sons of Ham, by their clans, by their languages, in their lands, in their nations.

10:21.en: Children were born to Shem also, the father of all the sons of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder.

10:22.en: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud and Aram.

10:23.en: The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.

10:24.en: Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

10:25.en: To Eber were born two sons. The name of the one was Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother was Joktan.

10:26.en: Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

10:29.en: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan.

10:3.en: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

10:30.en: Their homeland stretched from Mesha, as you go toward Sephar, to the eastern mountain.

10:31.en: These are the sons of Shem, by their clans, by their languages, in their lands, by their nations.

10:32.en: These are the clans of the sons of Noah, by their lineages, in their nations; and from these the nations were divided on the earth after the flood.

10:4.en: The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

10:5.en: From these the coastlands of the nations were separated in their lands, each according to its language, by their clans, in their nations.

10:6.en: The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.

10:7.en: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

10:8.en: Cush fathered Nimrod. He began to be a mighty man on the earth.

10:9.en: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.

11:1.en: Now the whole earth had one language and the same words.

11:10.en: These are the generations of Shem. Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered Arpachshad, two years after the flood.

11:11.en: And Shem lived, after he fathered Arpachshad, five hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:12.en: Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah.

11:13.en: Arpachshad lived, after he fathered Shelah, four hundred and three years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:14.en: Shelah lived thirty years, and he fathered Eber.

11:15.en: Shelah lived four hundred and three years after fathering Eber, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:16.en: Eber lived thirty-four years, and he fathered Peleg.

11:17.en: Eber lived four hundred and thirty years after fathering Peleg, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:18.en: Peleg lived thirty years, and he fathered Reu.

11:19.en: After he fathered Reu, Peleg lived two hundred nine years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:2.en: As they traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

11:20.en: Reu lived thirty-two years, and he fathered Serug.

11:21.en: After he fathered Serug, Reu lived two hundred seven years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:22.en: Serug lived thirty years, and he fathered Nahor.

11:23.en: Serug lived, after he fathered Nahor, two hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:24.en: Nahor lived twenty-nine years, and he fathered Terah.

11:25.en: Nahor lived, after he fathered Terah, one hundred nineteen years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

11:26.en: Terah lived seventy years, and he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

11:27.en: These are the generations of Terah: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.

11:28.en: Haran died in the lifetime of his father Terah, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.

11:29.en: Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. The name of Abram's wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahor's wife was Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was the father of Milcah and the father of Iscah.

11:3.en: They said to one another, "Come, let us make bricks and burn them hard." So brick served them as stone, and bitumen served them as mortar.

11:30.en: Sarai was barren; she had no child.

11:31.en: Terah took his son Abram, and Lot, the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of his son Abram, and they went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan; they came as far as Haran and settled there.

11:32.en: The days of Terah were two hundred and five years, and Terah died in Haran.

11:4.en: Then they said, "Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth."

11:5.en: The LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the children of the human were building.

11:6.en: The LORD said, "Look, they are one people with one language for all of them, and this is what they have begun to do. Now nothing will be held back from them that they plan to do."

11:7.en: "Come, let us go down and confuse their language there, so that they will not understand one another's language."

11:8.en: So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.

11:9.en: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.

12:1.en: The LORD said to Abram, "Go forth from your land, from your birthplace, and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you."

12:10.en: Now there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine in the land was severe.

12:11.en: As he drew near to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, "Look now, I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance.

12:12.en: When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife,’ and they will kill me, but you they will let live.

12:13.en: Say, please, that you are my sister, so that it may go well with me on your account, and I may live because of you.

12:14.en: When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

12:15.en: Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her for Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh's house.

12:16.en: And Pharaoh treated Abram well because of her, and he came to have flocks and herds, donkeys, male and female slaves, she-donkeys, and camels.

12:17.en: Then the LORD struck Pharaoh with great plagues, and his household too, on account of Sarai, Abram's wife.

12:18.en: Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she is your wife?"

12:19.en: Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her as my wife? Now, here is your wife: take her and go.

12:2.en: I will make you into a great nation, I will bless you, and make your name great, and you shall be a blessing.

12:20.en: Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him, and they escorted him on his way, together with his wife and all that was his.

12:3.en: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who curses you I will curse, and all the families of the earth will bless themselves by you.

12:4.en: So Abram went, as the LORD had spoken to him, and Lot went with him. Now Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

12:5.en: Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother's son, and all the property that they had amassed, and the people they had acquired in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan, and they came to the land of Canaan.

12:6.en: Abram passed through the land as far as the site of Shechem, as far as the terebinth of Moreh. The Canaanite was then in the land.

12:7.en: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." So he built an altar there to the LORD who had appeared to him.

12:8.en: He moved his tent from there to the mountain east of Bethel and pitched it, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.

12:9.en: Abram set out, going on from stage to stage toward the Negeb.

13:1.en: So Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that was his, and Lot with him, to the Negeb.

13:10.en: Lot lifted up his eyes and saw the whole plain of the Jordan, that all of it was well watered, before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, as you come to Zoar.

13:11.en: Lot chose for himself the whole plain of the Jordan, and Lot set out from the east, and they separated, one from the other.

13:12.en: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent as far as Sodom.

13:13.en: Now the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners against the LORD, exceedingly.

13:14.en: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, "Lift your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward."

13:15.en: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.

13:16.en: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone can count the dust of the earth, then your offspring too can be counted.

13:17.en: Get up, walk about the land through its length and its breadth, for I will give it to you.

13:18.en: Abram moved his tent, came and settled at the terebinths of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built there an altar to the LORD.

13:2.en: Now Abram was very heavily laden with livestock, with silver and with gold.

13:3.en: He went on his journeys from the Negeb as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

13:4.en: to the place of the altar that he had made there at first; and there Abram called on the name of the LORD.

13:5.en: Also, Lot, who went with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.

13:6.en: But the land could not support them to live together, for their property was great, and they could not live together.

13:7.en: So there was a quarrel between the herders of Abram's livestock and the herders of Lot's livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites were then living in the land.

13:8.en: Abram said to Lot, "Please, let there be no quarrel between me and you, or between my herders and your herders, for we are kinsmen."

13:9.en: Is not the whole land before you? Please separate from me. If you go left, I will go right; and if you go right, I will go left.

14:1.en: It happened in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,

14:10.en: The Valley of Siddim was pit upon pit of bitumen, and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell there, and the survivors fled into the hills.

14:11.en: They took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and went away.

14:12.en: They took Lot, the son of Abram's brother, and his goods, and went away; he was living in Sodom.

14:13.en: The fugitive came and told Abram the Hebrew, who was living by the terebinths of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner; they were allies of Abram.

14:14.en: When Abram heard that his brother had been taken captive, he armed his trained men, those born in his household, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

14:15.en: He and his servants divided themselves against them by night and struck them, and pursued them as far as Hobah, which is north of Damascus.

14:16.en: He brought back all the goods, and also brought back Lot his brother and his goods, and also the women and the people.

14:17.en: The king of Sodom went out to meet him, after his return from striking down Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, to the Valley of Shaveh, that is, the King's Valley.

14:18.en: Now Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.

14:19.en: He blessed him and said, "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, maker of heaven and earth."

14:2.en: they made war on Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.

14:20.en: And blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand. And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.

14:21.en: The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself."

14:22.en: Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I raise my hand in oath to the LORD, God Most High, maker of heaven and earth:

14:23.en: I will not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap, nor anything that is yours, so that you cannot say, 'I made Abram rich.'

14:24.en: Not for me, only what my servants have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol and Mamre. They may take their share."

14:3.en: All these joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea.

14:4.en: For twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

14:5.en: In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came, and the kings who were with him, and they struck the Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim,

14:6.en: and the Horites in their mountain, Seir, as far as El-paran, which is by the wilderness.

14:7.en: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat, which is Kadesh, and struck all the territory of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.

14:8.en: Then the king of Sodom went out, and the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, and they drew up battle lines against them in the Valley of Siddim.

14:9.en: with Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: four kings against the five.

15:1.en: After these events the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying: Do not be afraid, Abram. I am a shield for you; your reward is very great.

15:10.en: He took all these for him, cut them in the middle, and set each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not cut in two.

15:11.en: The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them off.

15:12.en: As the sun was about to go down, a deep sleep fell on Abram, and suddenly dread, a great darkness, was falling on him.

15:13.en: He said to Abram, "Know for certain that your offspring will be sojourners in a land not theirs, and they will serve them, and they will oppress them, for four hundred years.

15:14.en: And also the nation that they will serve, I will judge; and afterward they will come out with great wealth.

15:15.en: As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.

15:16.en: And in the fourth generation they will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.

15:17.en: When the sun had set and it was thick darkness, there was a smoking furnace and a flaming torch that passed between these pieces.

15:18.en: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying: To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates:

15:19.en: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites;

15:2.en: Abram said, My Lord, the LORD, what will you give me, when I go on childless, and the steward of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?

15:20.en: the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim;

15:21.en: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.

15:3.en: Abram said, Look, you have given me no offspring, and so a member of my household is my heir.

15:4.en: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying: This man will not be your heir; but rather one who comes from your own body will be your heir.

15:5.en: He brought him outside and said, Look toward the sky, please, and count the stars, if you are able to count them. Then he said to him, So will your offspring be.

15:6.en: He trusted in the LORD, and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.

15:7.en: He said to him, I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to take possession of it.

15:8.en: He said, My Lord, the LORD, by what will I know that I shall take possession of it?

15:9.en: He said to him, "Take for me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old she-goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."

16:1.en: Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had not borne him a child. She had an Egyptian maidservant, and her name was Hagar.

16:10.en: The messenger of the LORD said to her, "I will greatly multiply your offspring, so that they cannot be counted for their multitude."

16:11.en: The messenger of the LORD said to her, "Here you are, pregnant: you will bear a son, and you are to name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your affliction."

16:12.en: He will be a wild ass of a man, his hand against everyone and everyone's hand against him, and he will dwell over against all his kin.

16:13.en: She called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, "You are El Roi," for she said, "Have I even here seen, after the one who sees me?"

16:14.en: Therefore the well is called Beer Lahai Roi; there it is, between Kadesh and Bered.

16:15.en: Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishmael.

16:16.en: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.

16:2.en: Sarai said to Abram, "Look, the LORD has kept me from bearing children. Please go in to my maidservant; perhaps I shall be built up through her." And Abram listened to Sarai's voice.

16:3.en: Then Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her maidservant, at the end of ten years of Abram's dwelling in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.

16:4.en: He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. She saw that she had conceived, and her mistress became of little account in her eyes.

16:5.en: Sarai said to Abram, "The wrong done to me is on you! I myself gave my maidservant into your arms, and when she saw that she had conceived, I became of little account in her eyes. May the LORD judge between me and you."

16:6.en: Abram said to Sarai, "Here, your maidservant is in your hand. Do to her what is good in your eyes." Then Sarai dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her presence.

16:7.en: Then the angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.

16:8.en: He said, "Hagar, maidservant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" She said, "I am fleeing from Sarai my mistress."

16:9.en: The messenger of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress, and submit to her authority."

17:1.en: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him, "I am El Shaddai. Walk before me and be whole."

17:10.en: This is my covenant, which you shall keep between me and you and between your offspring after you: every male among you is to be circumcised.

17:11.en: You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be a sign of covenant between me and you.

17:12.en: At eight days old every male among you is to be circumcised, throughout your generations: the one born in the house, or bought with money from any foreigner who is not of your offspring.

17:13.en: The one born in your house and the one bought with your money must be circumcised, and my covenant shall be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.

17:14.en: Any uncircumcised male who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, that person shall be cut off from his kin; he has broken my covenant.

17:15.en: God said to Abraham, "Sarai your wife: do not call her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name."

17:16.en: I will bless her, and I will also give you a son from her. I will bless her, and she shall become nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.

17:17.en: Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, "Will a child be born to a man a hundred years old? And will Sarah, a woman of ninety years, bear a child?"

17:18.en: Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live before you!"

17:19.en: God said, "Truly, Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac; and I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him."

17:2.en: I will set my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.

17:20.en: As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Look, I have blessed him and will make him fruitful and will increase him exceedingly. He will father twelve chieftains, and I will make him a great nation.

17:21.en: But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear for you at this appointed time next year.

17:22.en: When he had finished speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

17:23.en: Then Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his house and all those bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham's household, and he circumcised the flesh of their foreskin on that very day, as God had spoken with him.

17:24.en: Now Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised, in the flesh of his foreskin.

17:25.en: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

17:26.en: On that very day Abraham was circumcised, and Ishmael his son.

17:27.en: And all the men of his household, those born in the house and those bought with money from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.

17:3.en: Abram fell on his face, and God spoke with him, saying:

17:4.en: As for me, here is my covenant with you: you shall become the father of a multitude of nations.

17:5.en: No longer shall your name be called Abram; your name shall be Abraham, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.

17:6.en: I will make you exceedingly fruitful, and I will make you into nations, and kings shall come forth from you.

17:7.en: I will establish my covenant between me and you and between your offspring after you, throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.

17:8.en: I will give to you and to your offspring after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.

17:9.en: God said to Abraham, "As for you, you shall keep my covenant, you and your offspring after you, throughout their generations."

1:1.en: When God began to create the heavens and the earth —

1:10.en: God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering of the waters he called Seas. God saw that it was good.

1:11.en: God said, "Let the earth sprout green growth, plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit, each of its own kind, with its seed in it, on the earth." And it was so.

1:12.en: The earth brought forth green growth, plants yielding seed, each of its own kind, and trees bearing fruit with its seed in it, each of its own kind. God saw that it was good.

1:13.en: There was evening and there was morning, a third day.

1:14.en: God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to separate the day from the night, and let them be for signs and for appointed times, and for days and years,

1:15.en: and let them be lights in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth." And it was so.

1:16.en: God made the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night, and the stars.

1:17.en: God set them in the expanse of the sky to give light on the earth.

1:18.en: and to rule over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.

1:19.en: There was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

1:2.en: the earth was desolate and empty, with darkness over the face of the deep and the wind of God hovering over the face of the waters —

1:20.en: And God said, "Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the expanse of the sky."

1:21.en: And God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

1:22.en: And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the land."

1:23.en: And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

1:24.en: God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures, each according to its kind: livestock and crawling things and the wild animals of the earth, each according to its kind." And so it was.

1:25.en: God made the wild animals of the earth, each according to its kind, and the livestock according to its kind, and every crawling thing of the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.

1:26.en: God said, "Let us make humankind in our image, after our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and the livestock and all the earth and every crawling thing that crawls on the earth."

1:27.en: God created the human in his image; in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

1:28.en: God blessed them, and God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and every living thing that crawls on the earth."

1:29.en: God said, "See, I have given you every plant bearing seed that is on the surface of the whole earth, and every tree that has in it fruit of a tree bearing seed. It shall be yours for food."

1:3.en: God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.

1:30.en: And to every wild animal of the earth and to every bird of the sky and to everything that crawls on the earth, in which there is a living soul, I have given every green plant for food. And so it was.

1:31.en: God saw everything that he had made, and indeed it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.

1:4.en: God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.

1:5.en: God called the light day, and the darkness he called night. There was evening and there was morning, one day.

1:6.en: God said, "Let there be an expanse in the middle of the waters, and let it divide water from water."

1:7.en: God made the expanse and divided the water below the expanse from the water above the expanse. And it was so.

1:8.en: God called the expanse Sky. There was evening and there was morning, a second day.

1:9.en: God said, "Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear." And it was so.

2:1.en: So the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their host.

2:10.en: A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides and becomes four headwaters.

2:11.en: The name of the first is Pishon; it is the one that encircles the whole land of Havilah, where the gold is.

2:12.en: The gold of that land is good; bdellium is there, and onyx stone.

2:13.en: The name of the second river is Gihon; it is the one that encircles the whole land of Cush.

2:14.en: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it is the one that flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

2:15.en: The LORD God took the human and set him in the garden of Eden to work it and guard it.

2:16.en: The LORD God commanded the human, saying: "You may eat freely from every tree of the garden.

2:17.en: But from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you must not eat from it, for on the day you eat from it you will surely die.

2:18.en: The LORD God said, "It is not good for the human to be alone; I will make for him a helper corresponding to him."

2:19.en: The LORD God formed from the ground every animal of the field and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the human to see what he would call it. Whatever the human called each living creature, that was its name.

2:2.en: On the seventh day God finished his work that he had made, and on the seventh day he rested from all his work that he had made.

2:20.en: The human gave names to all the livestock and the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the field; but for himself the human did not find a helper corresponding to him.

2:21.en: Then the LORD God cast a deep sleep upon the human, and he slept; and he took one of his sides and closed up flesh in its place.

2:22.en: The LORD God built the side that he had taken from the human into a woman, and brought her to the human.

2:23.en: Then the human said, "This one, this time, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. This one shall be called woman, for from man this one was taken."

2:24.en: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.

2:25.en: The two of them were naked, the human and his wife, and they were not ashamed.

2:3.en: God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all his work that God created in order to make.

2:4.en: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day the LORD God made earth and heavens.

2:5.en: No tree of the field was yet on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for the LORD God had not sent rain on the earth, and there was no human to work the ground.

2:6.en: But a mist rose from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.

2:7.en: Then the LORD God formed the human out of dust from the ground, and blew into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human became a living being.

2:8.en: The LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and put there the human whom he had formed.

2:9.en: The LORD God made grow from the ground every tree desirable to look at and good for food, and the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

3:1.en: Now the serpent was shrewder than every wild animal that the LORD God had made. It said to the woman, “Is it really so that God said, ‘You must not eat from any tree of the garden’?”

3:10.en: He said, "I heard your sound in the garden, and I was afraid because I am naked, and I hid."

3:11.en: He said, "Who told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?"

3:12.en: The human said, "The woman whom you put with me, she gave me from the tree, and I ate."

3:13.en: The LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."

3:14.en: The LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you more than all the livestock and more than all the wild animals of the field. On your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life."

3:15.en: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.

3:16.en: To the woman he said, “I will greatly multiply your pain and your pregnancy; in pain you will bear children. Your desire is for your husband, and he will rule over you.”

3:17.en: And to Adam he said, “Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, saying, ‘You will not eat from it,’ cursed is the ground because of you; in toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.

3:18.en: It will sprout thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.

3:19.en: By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken; for you are dust, and to dust you will return.

3:2.en: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat from the fruit of the trees of the garden.”

3:20.en: The human called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all the living.

3:21.en: The LORD God made tunics of skin for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.

3:22.en: The LORD God said, "Look, the human has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever."

3:23.en: So the LORD God expelled him from the garden of Eden to work the ground from which he was taken.

3:24.en: He drove out the human, and east of the garden of Eden he stationed the cherubim and the flame of the turning sword, to guard the way to the tree of life.

3:3.en: As for the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, “You must not eat from it, and you must not touch it, or you might die.”

3:4.en: The serpent said to the woman, “You will certainly not die.”

3:5.en: For God knows that on the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like divine beings, knowing good and evil.

3:6.en: The woman saw that the tree was good for eating, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable for gaining insight. She took some of its fruit and ate, and she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.

3:7.en: Then the eyes of the two of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves loincloths.

3:8.en: They heard the sound of the LORD God walking about in the garden at the breeze of the day, and the human and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden.

3:9.en: The LORD God called to the human and said to him, "Where are you?"

4:1.en: Now the human had known Eve his wife, and she had conceived and borne Cain, and she said, "I have acquired a man with the LORD."

4:10.en: He said, "What have you done? Listen: the blood of your brother is crying out to me from the ground."

4:11.en: And now you are cursed from the ground, which opened its mouth to take your brother's blood from your hand.

4:12.en: When you work the ground, it will no longer give you its strength. You shall be a restless wanderer on the earth.

4:13.en: Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is too great to bear."

4:14.en: Look, you have driven me out today from the face of the ground, and from your presence I will be hidden. I will be restless and wandering on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.

4:15.en: Then the LORD said to him, "Therefore, whoever kills Cain—! After seven generations vengeance will be taken." And the LORD set a sign for Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him down.

4:16.en: Then Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

4:17.en: Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. He was building a city, and he named the city after his son Enoch.

4:18.en: To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.

4:19.en: Lamech took for himself two wives: the name of the first was Adah, and the name of the second Zillah.

4:2.en: She went on to bear his brother, Abel. Abel was a herder of flocks, and Cain was a worker of the ground.

4:20.en: Adah bore Jabal; he was the first of those who live in tents and have livestock.

4:21.en: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the first of all who handle the lyre and the pipe.

4:22.en: Zillah too bore Tubal-cain, who sharpened every tool of the craft in bronze and iron; and Tubal-cain's sister was Naamah.

4:23.en: Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech: have I killed a man by my wounding, a boy by my bruising?"

4:24.en: For if vengeance is taken on Cain sevenfold, then on Lamech seventy-seven.

4:25.en: Adam was intimate once more with his wife, and she bore a son and named him Seth, "for God has appointed me another offspring in place of Abel, because Cain killed him."

4:26.en: To Seth, too, a son was born, and he named him Enosh. Then people began to call on the name of the LORD.

4:3.en: At the end of a year, Cain brought an offering of the fruit of the ground to the LORD.

4:4.en: And Abel brought, he too, some of the firstlings of his flock and of their fat portions. And the LORD turned to Abel and to his offering,

4:5.en: but to Cain and to his offering he did not turn. And Cain was very angry, and his face fell.

4:6.en: The LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?"

4:7.en: Is it not so that if you do well, there is forgiveness, and if you do not do well, at the door sin crouches? Its desire is for you, but you can rule over it.

4:8.en: Cain spoke to Abel his brother. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.

4:9.en: The LORD said to Cain, "Where is Abel your brother?" He said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"

5:1.en: This is the record of the descendants of Adam. When God created Adam, he made him in the likeness of God.

5:10.en: After he fathered Kenan, Enosh lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:11.en: All the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.

5:12.en: Kenan lived seventy years, and he fathered Mahalalel.

5:13.en: After he fathered Mahalalel, Kenan lived eight hundred and forty years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:14.en: All the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.

5:15.en: Mahalalel lived sixty-five years, and he fathered Jared.

5:16.en: After he fathered Jared, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:17.en: All the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.

5:18.en: Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and fathered Enoch.

5:19.en: Jared lived, after he fathered Enoch, for eight hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:2.en: Male and female he created them, and he blessed them and called their name Adam, on the day they were created.

5:20.en: All the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.

5:21.en: Enoch lived sixty-five years, and fathered Methuselah.

5:22.en: Enoch walked with God, after he fathered Methuselah, for three hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:23.en: All the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.

5:24.en: Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him.

5:25.en: Methuselah lived one hundred eighty-seven years, and he fathered Lamech.

5:26.en: Methuselah lived, after he fathered Lamech, seven hundred eighty-two years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:27.en: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, and he died.

5:28.en: Lamech lived one hundred eighty-two years, and he fathered a son.

5:29.en: He named him Noah, saying, "This one will bring us relief from our work and from the toil of our hands, from the ground that the LORD has cursed."

5:3.en: Adam lived one hundred thirty years, and he fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image, and named him Seth.

5:30.en: Lamech lived, after he fathered Noah, five hundred ninety-five years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:31.en: All the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy-seven years, and he died.

5:32.en: When Noah was five hundred years old, Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

5:4.en: The days of Adam after he fathered Seth were eight hundred years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:5.en: So all the days of Adam that he lived were nine hundred thirty years, and he died.

5:6.en: Seth lived one hundred and five years, and he fathered Enosh.

5:7.en: After he fathered Enosh, Seth lived eight hundred and seven years, and he fathered sons and daughters.

5:8.en: All the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.

5:9.en: Enosh lived ninety years, and he fathered Kenan.

6:1.en: When humankind began to multiply over the surface of the ground and daughters were born to them,

6:10.en: Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6:11.en: The earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.

6:12.en: God saw the earth, and indeed it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.

6:13.en: God said to Noah, "The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is full of violence because of them; now I am about to destroy them with the earth."

6:14.en: Make yourself an ark of gopher wood; make the ark with compartments, and cover it with pitch inside and out.

6:15.en: This is how you shall make it: the ark's length shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.

6:16.en: Make a skylight for the ark, and finish it off to a cubit at the top. Set the door of the ark in its side; make it with lower, second, and third stories.

6:17.en: As for me, I am about to bring the flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens; everything that is on the earth shall perish.

6:18.en: I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall enter the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.

6:19.en: And of every living thing, of all flesh, you shall bring two of each into the ark to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.

6:2.en: The sons of the rulers saw that the daughters of humankind were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves from all whom they chose.

6:20.en: Of the birds according to their kind, and of the animals according to their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of each will come to you to be kept alive.

6:21.en: As for you, take for yourself some of every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself, so that it will be food for you and for them.

6:22.en: Noah did according to all that God had commanded him; so he did.

6:3.en: Then the LORD said, "My spirit will not contend over humankind for long, since they are also flesh; their days will be one hundred and twenty years."

6:4.en: The giants were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, whenever the sons of the rulers came to the daughters of humankind and they bore children to them. They were the warriors of old, the men of renown.

6:5.en: The LORD saw that the evil of the human was great on the earth, and every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil all day long.

6:6.en: The LORD regretted that he had made the human on the earth, and was grieved in his heart.

6:7.en: The LORD said, "I will wipe out the human whom I created from the face of the ground, from human to beast, to creeping thing, and to the birds of the sky, for I regret that I made them."

6:8.en: But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

6:9.en: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generations; Noah walked with God.

7:1.en: Then the LORD said to Noah: Come, you and all your household, into the ark, for I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.

7:10.en: And when the seven days were over, the waters of the flood were on the earth.

7:11.en: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the sky were opened.

7:12.en: And the rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.

7:13.en: On that very day Noah went in, and Shem and Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and the wife of Noah and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark.

7:14.en: They and every wild animal according to its kind, and every domestic animal according to its kind, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind, every bird of every kind of wing.

7:15.en: They came to Noah, into the ark, two by two from all flesh in which there was the breath of life.

7:16.en: Those that came in, male and female from all flesh, came in as God had commanded him, and the LORD shut him in.

7:17.en: When the flood had lasted forty days on the earth, the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.

7:18.en: The waters grew strong and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark moved on the surface of the waters.

7:19.en: The waters prevailed very, very greatly on the earth, and all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.

7:2.en: Of every clean animal take for yourself seven each, a male and his mate; and of the animals that are not clean, two, a male and his mate.

7:20.en: Fifteen cubits upward the waters prevailed, and the mountains were covered.

7:21.en: All flesh that moved on the earth had perished, among birds and livestock and wild animals and among every swarming thing that swarms on the earth, and all humankind.

7:22.en: Everything that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, of all that was on dry land, died.

7:23.en: He wiped out every living thing that was on the surface of the ground, from humans to animals, to crawling things, and to the birds of the sky; they were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.

7:24.en: The waters prevailed over the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

7:3.en: Also of the birds of the sky, seven each, male and female, to keep seed alive across the face of all the earth.

7:4.en: For in seven more days I will make it rain on the earth forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe out every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground.

7:5.en: Noah did according to all that the LORD had commanded him.

7:6.en: Now Noah was six hundred years old when the flood came, water upon the earth.

7:7.en: Noah went into the ark, and his sons and his wife and his sons' wives with him, because of the waters of the flood.

7:8.en: Of the clean animals, and of the animals that are not clean, and of the birds, and of everything that creeps on the ground,

7:9.en: two by two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.

8:1.en: God remembered Noah and every living creature and all the domestic animals that were with him in the ark, and God made a wind pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

8:10.en: He waited another seven days, and again he sent the dove away from the ark.

8:11.en: The dove came to him at evening time, and there in her beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters had abated from the earth.

8:12.en: He waited another seven days and sent the dove away, and she did not return to him any more.

8:13.en: In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first of the month, the waters dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and there the surface of the ground had dried up.

8:14.en: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.

8:15.en: Then God spoke to Noah, saying:

8:16.en: Go out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and your sons' wives with you.

8:17.en: Bring out with you every living creature that is with you, of all flesh, birds and animals and everything that creeps on the earth, and let them breed abundantly on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.

8:18.en: So Noah went out, with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.

8:19.en: All the animals, all the creeping things, and all the birds, everything that moves on the earth, went out of the ark by their kinds.

8:2.en: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the sky were shut, and the rain from the sky was held back.

8:20.en: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and he took some of every clean animal and every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

8:21.en: The LORD smelled the soothing aroma, and the LORD said to himself, "I will never again curse the ground because of the human, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from his youth; and I will never again strike down every living thing as I have done."

8:22.en: For as long as the earth lasts, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease.

8:3.en: The waters withdrew from the earth steadily, and the waters decreased at the end of a hundred and fifty days.

8:4.en: The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.

8:5.en: The waters continued to diminish steadily until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains became visible.

8:6.en: At the end of forty days Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.

8:7.en: He sent out the raven, and it went back and forth until the waters had dried from off the earth.

8:8.en: Then he sent the dove away from him, to see whether the waters had abated from the surface of the ground.

8:9.en: But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned to him, to the ark, for there was water over the surface of all the earth. So he stretched out his hand, took her, and brought her to him into the ark.

9:1.en: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth."

9:10.en: and with every living creature that is with you, among the birds, among the livestock, and among every animal of the earth that is with you, from all that came out of the ark, to every animal of the earth.

9:11.en: I will establish my covenant with you: never again will any flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.

9:12.en: Then God said: This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between me and you and between every living creature that is with you, for everlasting generations.

9:13.en: I have now set my bow in the cloud, and it will become a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.

9:14.en: When I bring clouds over the earth, the bow will appear in the cloud.

9:15.en: I will remember my covenant that is between me and you and between every living creature among all flesh, and never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.

9:16.en: The bow will be in the cloud, and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living being, among all flesh that is on the earth.

9:17.en: God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh that is on the earth."

9:18.en: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.

9:19.en: These three were the sons of Noah, and from these the whole earth was dispersed.

9:2.en: The fear and dread of you shall be upon every animal of the earth and upon every bird of the sky, upon everything that crawls on the ground and upon all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are given.

9:20.en: Noah, a man of the soil, began and planted a vineyard.

9:21.en: He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and uncovered himself inside his tent.

9:22.en: Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

9:23.en: Shem and Japheth took the garment and laid it on both their shoulders, and they walked backward and covered their father's nakedness, and their faces were backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.

9:24.en: Noah woke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him.

9:25.en: He said, "Cursed be Canaan; a slave among slaves shall he be to his brothers."

9:26.en: He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem, and may Canaan be a slave to them."

9:27.en: May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and may Canaan be a slave to them.

9:28.en: After the flood Noah lived three hundred and fifty years.

9:29.en: All the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

9:3.en: Every moving thing that is alive shall be food for you; as with the green plants, I have given you everything.

9:4.en: Only flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.

9:5.en: But your blood, for your lives, I will demand; from every animal I will demand it, and from the human, from each man for his brother, I will demand the life of the human.

9:6.en: Whoever sheds the blood of the human, by the human his blood shall be shed; for in the image of God He made the human.

9:7.en: As for you, be fruitful and multiply; swarm over the earth and multiply in it.

9:8.en: Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him:

9:9.en: As for me, I am establishing my covenant with you and with your offspring after you,
